title: Finite-type spreading of a specified pinned split reductive realization
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be an extension of fields, let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee,\Delta)$ be a finite reduced based root datum, and let $P_K=(G_K,T_K=D_K(M),(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Delta})$ be a pinned split realization of $\mathcal R$ over $K$, with all notions as in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. There exist a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra $A\subseteq K$, a pinned split realization $P_A$ over $A$ of the same abstract based datum, and a pinning-compatible isomorphism $(P_A)_K\simeq P_K$ inducing the identity on $M$. Here $(P_A)_K$ means pullback along $A\hookrightarrow K$ as in [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change]. The model is reductive on all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, its torus is exactly $D_A(M)$, and its root lines are free of rank one over $A$. No spanning condition on $\Phi$, algebraicity of $K/k$, or positive-rank condition is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.12, first paragraph of proof, printed p.211: descent of the split triple to a finite-type Q-subalgebra of C. General field-extension version with finitely many pinning vectors and their basis identities included in the finite-presentation data. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states preservation of the split reductive structure in this spreading theorem.

proof.text: Order the finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $A_i\subseteq K$ by inclusion. They form a small directed set: adjoin the union of two finite generating sets for an upper bound. Their union is $K$, since each $x\in K$ belongs to $k[x]$. This union is the ring colimit (a compatible family of maps defines its unique map element by element). Every $A_i$ is a nonzero domain. The affine limit is consequently $\operatorname{Spec}K$ by the cited affine-limit theorem. Choose a basis of the finite-rank lattice $M$, so $A_i[M]$ has the fixed Laurent presentation $A_i[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, also when $r=0$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.12, first proof paragraph, p.211; affine-limit identification: Stacks Tags 01YX, 01YW.

proof.text: Write $G_K=\operatorname{Spec}B_K$. Choose a finite polynomial presentation of $B_K$ and adjoin its coefficients to $k$; the same presentation defines $B_i$ with $K\otimes_{A_i}B_i\simeq B_K$. Apply the algebra-map descent and equality clauses to descend the comultiplication $B_K\to B_K\otimes_K B_K$, counit $B_K\to K$, antipode $B_K\to B_K$, and torus restriction $B_K\to K[M]$. All tensor powers used here are finitely presented by the cited tensor-product lemma. The finitely many coassociativity, counit, antipode, and torus-homomorphism identities hold at a common later stage by the equality clause. Affine spectrum functoriality and the tensor pushout description of affine products turn these identities into precisely the group and homomorphism diagrams. Thus $G_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is an affine finitely presented group, with $j_i:D_{A_i}(M)\to G_i$, and its specified $K$-isomorphism is an isomorphism of groups restricting to the original torus map.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.12, p.211, expansion of finite-presentation descent; Stacks Tag 05N9 (2),(3), label lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, and Tags 00F4, 05G5.

proof.text: Make $j_i$ a closed immersion as follows. The map $B_K\to K[M]$ is surjective. For each of the finitely many Laurent generators $z_a,z_a^{-1}$ choose a preimage, written as a polynomial in the generators of $B_K$. Adjoin the finitely many coefficients of these polynomials to $A_i$. The equations that their images are $z_a,z_a^{-1}$ hold after a further enlargement: these are finitely many polynomial equations in $A_j[M]$, whose coefficients vanish in the injective subring map $A_j\hookrightarrow K$. Hence $B_j\to A_j[M]$ is surjective. Its spectrum is the closed subscheme cut out by its kernel, and it is a subgroup by the descended group identities. For $r=0$ the target is $A_j$, already generated as an $A_j$-algebra by its scalars.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.12, p.211, keeping the specified split torus; explicit finite Laurent-generator argument.

proof.text: The structure morphism $G_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is locally of finite presentation between affine qcqs schemes, with smooth $K$-pullback. Apply smoothness descent to the affine inverse system in step 1, and replace $i$ by that stage. Apply the new reductivity limit lemma to this now smooth affine finite-presentation group. Its $K$-pullback is the given reductive $G_K$, so at a later stage $G_i$ is reductive on the entire base. These two uses distinguish smoothness from the connected-reductive-geometric-fibre requirement; finite presentation alone would not give the latter.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0C0C, label lemma-descend-smooth; Conrad Corollary 3.1.11, pp.88--89.

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A_i)\subseteq K$ and $\eta\in\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ its generic point. The reductive $F$-group is smooth connected affine of finite type. Under $F\subseteq K$, the torus $T_F$ becomes the specified torus $T_K$, whose geometric fibre over an algebraic closure $\bar K$ is maximal. The field-extension theorem for $K\subseteq\bar K$ gives $T_K$ maximal in $G_K$; for $F\subseteq K$ it then says $T_F$ is maximal, and also geometrically maximal by applying that theorem to an algebraic closure of $F$. The torus-fibre openness theorem now supplies an open neighbourhood $V$ of $\eta$ on which $j_i$ is fibrewise maximal. Choose $0\ne f\in A_i$ with $\eta\in D(f)\subseteq V$ and replace $A_i$ by $A_i[1/f]\subseteq K$. This remains finitely generated over $k$ (adjoin $f^{-1}$); the group remains reductive because its geometric fibres are geometric fibres of the previous model. The torus is still exactly $D_{A_i}(M)$ and is maximal in every geometric fibre.

source.place: Conrad Proposition 3.1.9(2), pp.85--86; Milne, Algebraic Groups, Theorem 17.82, p.379.

proof.text: The ring $A_i$ is Noetherian by the finite-type-algebra theorem, since every ideal of the field $k$ is either $0$ or $k$. Apply the tangent-weight theorem to conjugation by $D_{A_i}(M)$, using the chosen basis $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r$. It gives $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_m\mathfrak g_m$, finite support, finite projective summands and arbitrary-base-change comparisons. In particular the nonzero $K$-weights have support exactly $\Phi$, and each root summand is the given one-dimensional line; the zero-weight summand is allowed to vanish. A finite projective module is finitely presented explicitly: write it as $\operatorname{im}p$ for an idempotent matrix on $A_i^n$, presented by the $n$ generators and the $n$ columns of $1-p$ as relations. This verifies the finite-presentation hypothesis for the next step.

source.place: Conrad Section 4 introduction, p.107; Stacks Tag 00FN, label lemma-Noetherian-permanence; finite-idempotent presentation written explicitly.

proof.text: For every $\alpha\in\Phi$, choose an isomorphism $K\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_{A_i}\mathfrak g_\alpha$, choosing $1\mapsto X_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Delta$. For every other nonzero weight in the finite support choose the isomorphism $K\otimes\mathfrak g_m\simeq0$. Use the module-map descent theorem on the directed tail of finite-type subalgebras containing $A_i$: descend each chosen map and its inverse, then descend both inverse identities by the equality clause. Only finitely many maps and equalities occur, so one common stage works. Tangent-weight base change identifies their targets with the root-weight modules of the new model. Thus all prescribed root lines are free of rank one, every unwanted nonzero weight vanishes, and the chosen simple-root basis vectors pull back to the specified $X_\alpha$, rather than merely to unspecified nonzero multiples. Reductivity and fibrewise maximality persist because geometric fibres of a pullback are geometric fibres over extensions of the earlier residue fields.

source.place: Conrad Proposition 6.2.12, p.211, with the specified pinning retained; Stacks Tag 01ZR, label lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, affine map and equality clauses.

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-base root-line and coroot theorem to the resulting reductive model with its closed fibrewise maximal split torus. It identifies $\mathfrak g_0=\operatorname{Lie}(T)$, so the weight decomposition has exactly the required zero summand. On every geometric fibre the nonzero weights, already proved to be precisely $\Phi$, are its roots. For each $\alpha\in\Phi$, the same theorem supplies its canonical relative coroot, represented by a locally constant function $\operatorname{Spec}A\to M^\vee$. The spectrum of the domain $A$ is connected, hence this function is constant. Its value after $A\hookrightarrow K$ is the prescribed $\alpha^\vee$ by the theorem's base-change clause and the original $K$-realization. Therefore every geometric fibre has exactly the prescribed corresponding coroots. This checks coroots as integer cocharacters, not as differentials, including in small characteristic.

source.place: Conrad Section 4, pp.107--109, Theorem 4.2.6, pp.120--121, and Definition 5.1.1, p.136.

proof.text: Equip the final $A$-model with the unchanged abstract base $\Delta$ and the descended generators. Steps 4--8 verify every condition in the definition of a pinned split realization. The specified group isomorphism over $K$ from step 2 identifies its torus with the originally identified $D_K(M)$, and step 7 identifies each named pinning vector. By the pinned base-change statement this is a pinning-compatible isomorphism $(P_A)_K\simeq P_K$ inducing the identity on $M$. All enlargements adjoined finitely many elements of $K$, including inverses of nonzero elements, so $A$ is still a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra of $K$. Empty $\Phi$, rank zero and a non-spanning root set require no modification: empty choices disappear and the central torus is retained.

source.place: Conrad Definitions 5.1.1 and 6.1.1, pp.136 and 186; final assembly of Proposition 6.2.12 spreading step.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of Proposition 6.2.12 first paragraph, p.211, using Corollary 3.1.11, Proposition 3.1.9, and the stated Stacks descent lemmas; specified pinning retained. Local Conrad copy WANTED.
